RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 50

An all-male panel is not conclusive proof of bias, as it may simply reflect senior leadership demographics in the industry, but unconscious bias—such as weighting subjective "client relationships" over technical seniority—is a plausible factor. 

Before alleging bias, follow up politely on your request for written feedback. Focus your inquiries objectively on scoring rubrics, competencies, and specific selection criteria rather than panel demographics. Directly challenging the panel's gender composition at this stage risks immediate defensiveness and burning professional bridges. If their explanation reveals shifting criteria, double standards, or persistent refusal to provide feedback, you can then consult HR or an employment specialist to determine whether to pursue formal action.
